definition: Endemic means native to, and found characteristically only in, one particular place or region.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word endemic. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know endemic should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The blind cave salamander is endemic to a single limestone spring in the Dinaric karst.
Native says only that a species arose where it now lives, while endemic adds that it lives nowhere else.
Exclusive is the strongest way to put the same idea, and an endemic species is exclusive to its range by definition, which is why 'endemic to' is always followed by a place.

Homegrown describes what sprang up in the place itself rather than being imported -- homegrown talent, homegrown produce. Endemic is the biologist's far stronger claim: not just from here, but found here and nowhere else on earth.

Local means found in or belonging to the immediate area, the way a local bakery or a local bird is simply one you meet nearby. Every one of a region's species is local to it when you are in that region; endemic claims a species is found in that one place and no other.

Endemic means native to, and found characteristically only in, one particular place or region.
A botanist's survey of a Pacific archipelago lists 700 islands and one shrub with waxy, notched leaves.
That shrub grows on twelve square kilometres of a single volcanic slope on one island and, after forty years of searching, on no other island in the chain and nowhere else on earth.
Seeds planted elsewhere in the archipelago die within a season.
The shrub is endemic to that one slope.
A species restricted to twelve square kilometres of one island out of 700, and found nowhere else on earth, has exactly the narrow, place-bound distribution that endemic names.
Endemic is nearly always followed by 'to' plus a place, and its whole force is the restriction: found here and nowhere else.
Indigenous, among this unit's secondary words, is the broader term, meaning simply native to a place and used of peoples as well as species, without the found-nowhere-else claim that endemic makes.

endemic: Exclusive is the strongest way to put the same idea, and an endemic species is exclusive to its range by definition, which is why 'endemic to' is always followed by a place.
The mist frog of Mount Oroya was described by science only in 1998, though villagers on the mountain had known its evening whistle for generations.
Surveys since then have confirmed something remarkable: the frog is endemic to the mountain's summit cloud forest, a patch of habitat barely nine square kilometers.
Expeditions have searched forty similar peaks in the same range and never once heard the whistle.
That tiny world range is what makes conservationists nervous.
A species found in many places can lose one and survive; this one has no second address.
A single road project, drought, or fungus could erase the mist frog everywhere it exists, which is why the summit was declared a reserve in 2011.
